summary: Gives the preferred order of approaches in Windows modules (native cmdlets, .NET, WMI via CIM, COM, executables) and introduces #Requires and #AnsibleRequires statements for declaring module requirements.
questions: Should my Windows module call executables or use PowerShell cmdlets?
How do I declare requirements in a PowerShell module?

answer_card.title: Preferred approaches in Windows modules
answer_card.answer_md:
Prefer, in order:
1. Native cmdlets (`Remove-Item -Path C:\temp -Recurse`)
2. .NET classes
3. WMI via `New-CimInstance`
4. COM via `New-Object -ComObject`
5. Native executables (e.g. `Secedit.exe`)

Declare needs with `#Requires` / `#AnsibleRequires`, one per line, usually near the top.
